examples.en: We need classes that develop children's initiative.

examples.ko: 자발성 없이는 이 일을 오래 하기 어려워요.
examples.en: Without self-motivation, it is hard to keep doing this job for long.
If you only do what you are told, your initiative drops.
Volunteer work starts from one's own will.
The teacher respects the students' willingness to act on their own.

examples.ko: 회사에서 직원의 자발성을 끌어내기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to draw out employees' initiative at a company.

explain: 일상에서는 '자발적으로'처럼 '자발적' 형태가 더 많이 쓰여요. '자발성'은 교육이나 직장 이야기에서 '자발성을 키우다, 높이다'처럼 써요. 반대되는 말은 '타율성'이에요.
explain_en: In daily speech the form '자발적(으로)' is more common. '자발성' appears in talk about education or work, as in '자발성을 키우다' (to foster initiative). The opposite is '타율성' (acting under outside direction).

examples.en: I knocked my friend down while playing around.
The child running toward me almost knocked me over.
In ssireum, you win if you knock your opponent down.
The puppy jumped on Grandma and knocked her over.
I didn't mean to knock you down.

examples.ko: 바닥에 놓인 가방이 사람을 자빠뜨릴 수도 있어요.
examples.en: A bag left on the floor can trip someone.

explain: '넘어뜨리다'와 뜻은 같지만 더 거칠고 구어적인 느낌이에요. 스스로 넘어지는 '자빠지다'와 짝이라서, 남을 넘어지게 할 때 '자빠뜨리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '넘어뜨리다' but sounds rougher and more colloquial. It pairs with '자빠지다' (to fall over by oneself); use '자빠뜨리다' when you make someone else fall.

en: rich man; man of property; man of fortune

examples.en: He is a wealthy man who made money from real estate.
Wealthy people get investment advice separately.

examples.ko: 한 자산가가 학교에 큰 기부금을 냈어요.
examples.en: A wealthy man donated a large sum to the school.
I am not wealthy, but I save diligently.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 자산가를 위한 세금 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news had a story about taxes for the wealthy.
I heard he grew up without worries as a rich man's son.

explain: '부자'가 일상에서 가장 흔하고, '자산가'는 땅, 건물, 주식처럼 재산이 많은 사람을 말할 때 조금 격식 있게 써요. 뉴스나 금융 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '부자' is the everyday word; '자산가' sounds a bit more formal and fits people with lots of property, buildings or stocks. You often hear it in news and finance talk.

examples.ko: 선생님이 문제 푸는 방법을 자상히 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher kindly explained how to solve the problem.

examples.ko: 할머니는 제 이야기를 늘 자상히 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Grandma always listens to my stories with care.

examples.ko: 길을 모른다고 하니까 직원이 자상히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: When I said I didn't know the way, the staff member explained it patiently.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약 먹는 법을 자상히 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor carefully told me how to take the medicine.

examples.ko: 어머니가 편지에 안부를 자상히 적어 보내셨어요.
examples.en: My mother wrote about how she was doing in detail and sent the letter.

examples.ko: 모르는 부분은 제가 자상히 가르쳐 드릴게요.
examples.en: I will teach you the parts you don't know, step by step.

explain: '자세히'가 더 일상적이고 내용이 꼼꼼하다는 느낌이에요. '자상히'는 상대를 배려하며 친절하게 해 주는 태도가 같이 느껴져요. 주로 '자상히 알려 주다, 설명해 주다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '자세히' is the more common word and stresses thoroughness. '자상히' also carries a caring, kind attitude toward the listener. It often appears as '자상히 알려 주다' or '자상히 설명해 주다'.

examples.ko: 농촌 마을이 스스로 자생력을 키워야 해요.
examples.en: Rural villages need to build their own capacity to survive.

examples.ko: 이 풀은 자생력이 강해서 잘 죽지 않아요.
examples.en: This grass is hardy and doesn't die easily.

examples.ko: 작은 가게도 자생력이 없으면 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: Even a small shop won't last long without the strength to stand on its own.

examples.ko: 지원금만 받으면 자생력이 약해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you only rely on subsidies, your self-reliance can weaken.

examples.ko: 지역 경제의 자생력을 높일 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We are looking for ways to raise the local economy's self-reliance.

examples.ko: 숲은 자생력이 있어서 시간이 지나면 다시 살아나요.
examples.en: A forest can recover on its own, so it comes back to life over time.

explain: 사람, 마을, 회사, 경제처럼 남의 도움 없이 스스로 살아남는 힘을 말할 때 써요. '자생력을 키우다, 기르다, 높이다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 식물이나 숲에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Used for people, villages, companies or economies that can survive without outside help. Common patterns are '자생력을 키우다/기르다/높이다', and it also works for plants and forests.

examples.en: The residents formed a grassroots group.
This movement started as a spontaneous trend.

examples.ko: 정부가 시킨 게 아니라 자생적 움직임이었어요.
examples.en: It wasn't ordered by the government; it was a spontaneous movement.
A homegrown culture takes time to form.
A self-generated order formed inside the market.

examples.ko: 그 동네에는 자생적 예술 단체가 많아요.
examples.en: That neighborhood has many homegrown art groups.

explain: 밖에서 시켜서가 아니라 그 안에서 저절로 생겨난 것에 써요. '자생적 모임'처럼 명사 앞에 오고, '자생적으로 생기다'나 '이 모임은 자생적이에요'처럼도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It describes things that arise from within rather than being imposed from outside. It goes before a noun as in '자생적 모임', and is also used as '자생적으로 생기다' or '자생적이에요'.

examples.en: A philanthropist donated books to the school.

examples.ko: 그분은 조용히 돕는 자선가로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as a quiet philanthropist.
Philanthropists gathered and raised a fund.
I want to become a philanthropist someday too.
With a benefactor's help, the children received scholarships.
I met a famous philanthropist and listened to his story.

explain: 돈이나 재능으로 어려운 사람을 꾸준히 돕는 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 말로 '기부자'는 한 번 낸 사람도 포함하고, '독지가'는 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used for people who steadily help those in need with money or talent. '기부자' (donor) can include someone who gave just once, and '독지가' is a more formal word.

en: make one's fortune by one's own efforts; succeed on one's own

examples.en: He started from nothing and made it on his own.
I read the story of a self-made businessman.

examples.ko: 부모님 도움 없이 자수성가하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to succeed without your parents' help.
I heard he made his own fortune and bought this building.
Building your own success takes a long time.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 자수성가한 분이라 아주 검소해요.
examples.en: My uncle is self-made, so he is very frugal.

explain: 물려받은 재산 없이 자기 힘으로 부와 지위를 이룬 사람에게 써요. 보통 '자수성가한 사람, 사업가'처럼 앞에서 꾸미는 모양으로 가장 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for someone who built wealth and status with no inheritance. It most often appears as a modifier, like '자수성가한 사람' or '자수성가한 사업가'.

examples.en: The celebrity apologized and went into a period of lying low.
Right now I need time for self-reflection and restraint.

examples.ko: 자숙 기간이 끝나면 다시 활동할 거예요.
examples.en: When the lying-low period ends, he will resume activities.

examples.ko: 그는 사고 이후 자숙하며 조용히 지냈어요.
examples.en: After the accident, he kept a low profile and stayed quiet.

examples.ko: 모두가 힘든 때라 파티는 자숙하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Since everyone is having a hard time, we decided to hold back on the party.
The city hall asked citizens to refrain from going out.

explain: 잘못이 있거나 분위기가 무거울 때 스스로 말과 행동을 조심하고 활동을 줄이는 것을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '자숙 기간, 자숙하다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means holding back on your words and actions yourself after a mistake or when the mood is heavy. In the news you often hear '자숙 기간' and '자숙하다'.

examples.en: I grew up in my mother's loving care.

examples.ko: 선생님은 자애가 가득한 눈으로 아이들을 보셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher looked at the children with eyes full of kindness.
A parent's love has no end.

examples.ko: 편지에 할머니의 자애에 감사하는 마음을 담았어요.
examples.en: I put my gratitude for Grandma's kindness into the letter.
People prayed, believing in God's mercy and love.
Her kindness was the same toward everyone.

explain: 부모, 스승, 신처럼 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 베푸는 깊고 따뜻한 사랑에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '사랑'이나 '정'이라고 하고, '자애'는 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It describes the deep, warm love that someone in a higher position, such as a parent, teacher or deity, gives to those below. In daily talk people just say '사랑' or '정'; '자애' shows up in writing and formal speech.

examples.en: Grandma's smile is truly warm and kind.
Thanks to the kind teacher, the children feel at ease.
She treats everyone with kindness.
His voice was so gentle that I felt relieved.
The kind priest welcomed the children.
I still remember my father's kind face.

explain: 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '자애로워요, 자애로운'으로 바뀌어요. '자상하다'보다 격식 있고, 어른이나 신이 아랫사람을 넓게 품는 느낌이 있어요. 높여야 하는 사람이 주어일 때는 '자애로우시다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: '자애로워요', '자애로운'. It is more formal than '자상하다' and suggests an elder or deity embracing those below. When the subject is someone to be honored, use '자애로우시다'.

examples.en: Books become nourishment for the mind.
Plants get nutrients from the soil.

examples.ko: 어릴 때의 경험이 지금 제 자양분이에요.
examples.en: My childhood experiences are what nourish me now.

examples.ko: 이 음식은 자양분이 풍부해서 아기에게 좋아요.
examples.en: This food is rich in nutrients, so it is good for babies.

examples.ko: 실패도 성장의 자양분이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even failure can be fuel for growth.
Fallen leaves rot and are used as nutrients for trees.

explain: 몸이나 식물의 영양을 말하기도 하지만, '마음의 자양분, 성장의 자양분'처럼 비유로 더 많이 써요. 음식 이야기에서는 보통 '영양분'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It can mean nutrients for a body or plant, but it is used even more figuratively, as in '마음의 자양분' or '성장의 자양분'. When talking about food, people usually say '영양분'.

examples.en: Morning fog lay thick over the village.
Smoke spread thickly through the room.

examples.ko: 먼지가 자욱이 일어서 눈을 뜰 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Dust rose so thickly that I couldn't open my eyes.
Clouds hang thick over the mountaintop.
Mist rose thickly along the river at dawn.
The kitchen is filled with thick steam.

explain: 안개, 연기, 먼지, 김이 공간에 가득 찬 모습에 써요. 주로 '자욱이 끼다, 깔리다, 퍼지다'처럼 말해요. 맞춤법은 '자욱히'가 아니라 '자욱이'예요.
explain_en: It describes fog, smoke, dust or steam filling a space. Typical phrases are '자욱이 끼다/깔리다/퍼지다'. The correct spelling is '자욱이', not '자욱히'.

examples.en: It is early morning, so the fog is thick.
I drove slowly along the fog-covered road.
The smoke was so thick that I couldn't see ahead.
I cleaned the storeroom that had been full of dust.

examples.ko: 안개가 자욱하게 낀 날에는 비행기가 늦게 떠요.
examples.en: On days when thick fog sets in, flights leave late.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 물안개가 자욱하더니 곧 사라졌어요.
examples.en: Mist hung thick over the lake and then soon disappeared.

explain: 안개, 연기, 먼지가 어떤 공간에 꽉 차 있을 때 써요. '짙다'는 농도에, '자욱하다'는 가득 퍼진 모습에 초점이 있어요. 부사는 '자욱이'예요.
explain_en: Use it when fog, smoke or dust fills a space. '짙다' focuses on density, while '자욱하다' focuses on how it spreads and fills the place. The adverb is '자욱이'.

examples.ko: 그 부모님은 자유방임 방식으로 아이를 키워요.
examples.en: Those parents raise their child in a hands-off way.

examples.ko: 자유방임 교육이 항상 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: A hands-off education isn't always good.

examples.ko: 회사가 자유방임 태도를 보이면 규칙이 무너져요.
examples.en: If a company takes a laissez-faire attitude, the rules fall apart.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 자유방임 정책에 대해 토론했어요.
examples.en: We debated laissez-faire policy in class.
I think leaving freedom to others and neglect are different.

examples.ko: 선생님은 자유방임보다 적당한 지도가 필요하다고 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher said that proper guidance is needed rather than total non-interference.

explain: 육아, 교육, 경제 이야기에서 간섭하지 않고 맡겨 두는 방식을 말할 때 써요. 좋은 뜻으로 쓰기도 하지만 '관리가 안 된다'는 비판의 느낌이 담길 때가 많아요. '자유방임주의'라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: Used in talk about parenting, education and economics for a hands-off approach. It can be neutral, but often carries a criticism that nobody is managing things. The term '자유방임주의' also exists.

examples.en: The government announced import liberalization.
Prices rose after price liberalization.

examples.ko: 여행 자유화가 되자 해외에 나가는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Once travel was liberalized, more people went abroad.

examples.ko: 시장 자유화에 찬성하는 사람도 있고 반대하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people support market liberalization and some oppose it.
Farmers are worried because of the liberalization measures.
When was the exchange rate liberalized?

explain: '수입 자유화, 가격 자유화'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여서 주로 뉴스와 경제 수업에서 나와요. 일상에서는 '규제를 풀다, 완화하다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It usually follows a field, as in '수입 자유화' or '가격 자유화', and appears mostly in news and economics classes. In everyday speech people often say '규제를 풀다' or '완화하다'.

examples.ko: 그 일은 알고 보니 본인의 자작극이었어요.
examples.en: It turned out that the whole thing was staged by the person himself.
There was a person who staged a stunt to become famous.
It came out that the theft report was a hoax.

examples.ko: 이 소문이 자작극 아니냐는 의심도 나와요.
examples.en: Some people suspect this rumor is staged.
The hoax was exposed, so he posted an apology.
I was fooled by my friend's setup and worried for a long time.

explain: 스스로 일을 꾸며 놓고 남이 한 것처럼 보이게 하는 일에 써요. '자작극을 벌이다, 꾸미다'로 자주 말하고, 뉴스나 SNS에서 '자작극 논란'처럼 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to staging something yourself and making it look like someone else's doing. Common phrases are '자작극을 벌이다/꾸미다', and '자작극 논란' appears often in news and social media.

examples.en: The writing is so tiny that it is hard to read.
There were lots of little tasks, so I was busy again today.
I picked up tiny shells at the beach.
Please chop the onion finely and add it.
The small worries I had are nothing now.
Even if the expenses are small, they add up to a lot.

explain: '작다'와 달리 작은 것들이 여럿 모여 있을 때 어울려요. '자잘한 글씨, 자잘한 일'처럼 쓰고, 일에 쓰면 '사소한'에 가까워요. 비슷한 말로 '자질구레하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike '작다', it fits when many small things are gathered together, as in '자잘한 글씨' or '자잘한 일'. Used for tasks it means 'trivial'. A similar word is '자질구레하다'.

examples.en: Mom puts the baby to sleep, softly singing 'jajang jajang'.
Hush-a-bye, my baby, go to sleep now.

examples.ko: 할머니가 자장자장 노래를 부르며 아기를 안아 줘요.
examples.en: Grandma holds the baby and sings a lullaby.

examples.ko: 아기가 울다가 자장자장 소리에 스르르 잠들었어요.
examples.en: The baby was crying, then drifted off to the sound of the lullaby.

examples.ko: 자장자장, 우는 건 그만하고 이제 눈을 감아요.
examples.en: Hush-a-bye, stop crying now and close your eyes.

examples.ko: 언니는 인형을 안고 자장자장 흉내를 내요.
examples.en: My older sister holds a doll and pretends to sing it a lullaby.

explain: 아기를 재울 때 달래듯 반복해서 말하는 소리예요. 노래는 '자장가'라고 하고, 어른들이 아이에게 말하거나 동화와 노래 가사에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is a soothing phrase repeated when putting a baby to sleep. The song itself is called a '자장가', and you hear it from adults talking to children and in fairy tales and song lyrics.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 자전적 이야기를 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel contains an autobiographical story.
The author published a new autobiographical essay.

examples.ko: 자전적 영화라서 감독의 어린 시절이 많이 나와요.
examples.en: It is an autobiographical film, so the director's childhood appears a lot.
It is a work with strong autobiographical elements.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 자전적 성격의 노래를 많이 써요.
examples.en: That singer writes many songs of an autobiographical nature.

examples.ko: 이번 책은 자전적 소설인데 허구도 꽤 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: This book is an autobiographical novel, but it has quite a bit of fiction mixed in.

explain: 작가나 감독이 자기 삶에서 이야기를 가져온 작품에 써요. '자전적 소설, 자전적 영화'처럼 명사 앞에 오고, '이 소설은 자전적이에요'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes works in which an author or director draws on their own life. It goes before nouns, as in '자전적 소설' or '자전적 영화', and can also be used as '자전적이에요'.

examples.en: It's a small house, but I live contentedly.
He is a person content with his present life.

examples.ko: 지금 성적에 자족하지 말고 계속 노력하세요.
examples.en: Don't settle for your current grades; keep trying.
His pay is small, but he is content, so he doesn't complain.
If you rest on a good result, you won't improve.
With a contented heart, you feel less anxious.

explain: 밖의 조건과 상관없이 지금 상태에 스스로 만족한다는 느낌이에요. 문맥에 따라 '자족하며 살다'처럼 좋은 뜻도 되고, '자족하면 발전이 없다'처럼 현재에 안주한다는 부정적인 뜻도 돼요.
explain_en: It suggests being satisfied with your current state regardless of outside conditions. Depending on context it can be positive ('자족하며 살다') or negative, meaning complacent ('자족하면 발전이 없다').

examples.ko: 요즘은 말과 행동을 조심하고 자중해야 해요.
examples.en: These days I have to be careful with my words and actions and act with restraint.
My senior told me to calm down and watch myself when I got worked up.

examples.ko: 큰 대회를 앞두고 선수들은 말과 행동을 자중하고 있어요.
examples.en: Ahead of the big tournament, the players are watching their words and actions.

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서는 자중하는 모습을 보여야 해요.
examples.en: In front of people, you should show that you act with restraint.

examples.ko: 자중하지 않으면 큰 실수를 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't keep yourself in check, you could make a big mistake.

examples.ko: 그는 인터뷰 후 자중하며 조용히 지냈어요.
examples.en: After the interview, he stayed quiet and kept himself in check.

explain: 말과 행동을 함부로 하지 않고 신중하게 조심한다는 뜻으로, 남에게 '자중하세요'라고 하면 경고하는 느낌이 강해요. '자숙'은 잘못한 뒤 활동을 줄이는 쪽이고, '자중'은 앞으로 조심하는 쪽에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It is about being careful and not acting rashly; telling someone '자중하세요' sounds like a firm warning. '자숙' is more about holding back after a mistake, while '자중' leans toward being careful going forward.

en: burst out shrieking; convulse (with laughter or crying); flinch in fright

examples.en: The baby was startled and burst into a shrieking cry.
Everyone burst into fits of laughter at my friend's joke.
The puppy jumped in fright at the thunder.
The roaring laughter could be heard all the way down the hall.

examples.ko: 주사를 맞자 아이가 자지러져서 달래느라 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The child shrieked at the shot, and it was hard to calm him.
The movie was so funny that I nearly died laughing.

explain: 소리가 갑자기 높고 크게 터져 나오는 모습에 써요. 주로 '자지러지게 울다, 웃다'로 말하고, 깜짝 놀라 몸이 움츠러드는 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a sound bursting out suddenly and loudly. It mostly appears as '자지러지게 울다/웃다' (to shriek or burst into laughter), and can also be used for flinching in fright.

en: guilty conscience; remorse; pangs of conscience

examples.ko: 실수한 뒤로 자책감에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: After my mistake, I couldn't sleep because of self-blame.
I feel guilty for not being able to help my friend.

examples.ko: 그는 오랫동안 큰 자책감을 안고 살아왔어요.
examples.en: He has lived for a long time carrying great guilt.
I didn't even want to eat because of the guilt.
Self-reproach gradually fades with time.

examples.ko: 아이를 크게 혼낸 뒤에 자책감이 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: After scolding my child harshly, a wave of regret came over me.

explain: 자기 잘못이나 부족함을 스스로 탓하는 마음이에요. '죄책감'은 잘못에 대한 죄스러움이고, '자책감'은 자신을 탓하는 데 초점이 있어요. '자책감이 들다, 느끼다, 시달리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of blaming yourself for your faults or shortcomings. '죄책감' is guilt over a wrongdoing, while '자책감' focuses on blaming yourself. Common patterns: '자책감이 들다/느끼다/시달리다'.

examples.ko: 계속 실패하자 그는 자포자기 상태가 됐어요.
examples.en: After failing again and again, he fell into a state of despair.
When you fall into despair, you don't feel like doing anything.
It is too early to give up on yourself.
Everyone was surprised by his I-don't-care answer.
I walked into the exam room with a hopeless feeling.
However hard it is, please don't just give up on yourself.

explain: '포기'는 어떤 일을 그만두는 것이고, '자포자기'는 절망해서 자신까지 내던진 듯 아무렇게나 하는 상태예요. '자포자기 상태, 자포자기식 태도'처럼 쓰고 동사는 '자포자기하다'예요.
explain_en: '포기' is quitting a particular thing, while '자포자기' is a state of despair where you stop caring about yourself and do things carelessly. It appears as '자포자기 상태' or '자포자기식 태도', and the verb is '자포자기하다'.

en: give oneself up; become desperate; abandon oneself

examples.en: Don't give up on yourself just because you failed once.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 걸 자포자기한 얼굴로 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat there with a face that had given up on everything.
I gave up on myself and didn't study at all.

examples.ko: 친구가 자포자기하는 걸 보니 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to see my friend in such despair.
If you give up on yourself, bigger problems arise.
Even if the test is hard, there is no need to despair.

explain: 희망을 잃고 스스로를 돌보지 않게 될 때 써요. 보통 '자포자기하지 마세요'처럼 위로하거나 말릴 때, 또는 '자포자기한 표정'처럼 모습을 설명할 때 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when someone loses hope and stops looking after themselves. It often appears in comfort or advice like '자포자기하지 마세요', or in descriptions like '자포자기한 표정'.

examples.en: That person does nothing but sing his own praises.
If the self-praise is excessive, it tires the listener.
This isn't boasting; it's a fact.

examples.ko: 발표 내용이 자화자찬으로 가득 차 있었어요.
examples.en: The presentation was full of self-congratulation.
At the meeting, the team leader started praising himself.

examples.ko: 자화자찬 같지만 제 요리 솜씨가 꽤 좋아요.
examples.en: It may sound like bragging, but I'm quite a good cook.

explain: 자기가 한 일을 스스로 칭찬하는 것인데, 듣는 사람이 민망할 만큼 지나칠 때 주로 써서 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 겸손하게 말하고 싶을 때 '자화자찬 같지만'이라고 먼저 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is praising your own work, usually when it is so excessive that listeners feel awkward, so it sounds negative. People also use '자화자찬 같지만' as a modest opener before saying something good about themselves.

examples.en: My friend who praises his own cooking is funny.
Don't boast too much; let's wait for the results.

examples.ko: 그는 발표 내내 자기 성과를 자화자찬했어요.
examples.en: He praised his own results throughout the presentation.
Working with someone who keeps praising himself is tiring.

examples.ko: 스스로 자화자찬하는 건 쑥스러워서 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm too shy to praise myself like that.
It's okay to pat yourself on the back once in a while.

explain: '자랑하다'보다 스스로 자기를 칭찬하는 모습이 두드러지고 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 하지만 가볍게 장난스러운 말투로 '자화자찬 좀 하자면'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Compared with '자랑하다', it stresses praising yourself and sounds negative. Still, people use it playfully, as in '자화자찬 좀 하자면' (if I may toot my own horn).

examples.ko: 장애인의 자활을 돕는 센터가 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new center that helps people with disabilities become self-supporting has opened.

examples.ko: 자활 의지가 강한 사람들이 많이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people with a strong will to stand on their own gathered.

examples.ko: 그는 자활에 성공해서 작은 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: He succeeded in becoming self-sufficient and opened a small shop.

examples.ko: 정부는 자활 지원 사업을 늘리고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is expanding its self-sufficiency support programs.

examples.ko: 자활을 위한 직업 교육을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: I am receiving job training for becoming self-supporting.

examples.ko: 도움을 받다가 자활로 이어진 경우도 많아요.
examples.en: There are many cases where receiving help led to self-sufficiency.

explain: 남의 도움에 기대지 않고 스스로 생계를 꾸려 가는 것을 말해요. 복지 뉴스에서 '자활 센터, 자활 지원'처럼 자주 나와요. '자립'은 더 넓게 독립하는 것이고, '자활'은 생계에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It means supporting your own livelihood without relying on others. It often appears in welfare news as '자활 센터' or '자활 지원'. '자립' is broader independence, while '자활' focuses on earning a living.
